newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus complains over alleged Turk Cypriot moves.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus complains over alleged Turk Cypriot moves.

text.p: Cyprus on Friday said it would protest against alleged Turkish Cypriot plans to prepare an empty Greek Cypriot town for settlement but the Turkish Cypriot administration denied making any preparations.

Acting President Spyros Kyprianou said at a news conference the government would send a letter to the U.N. secretary-general protesting against any plans to settle Turkish Cypriots in Varosha, which is in the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the divided island's north.
But Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash was quoted as saying the only plans for Varosha -- which Turks call Maras -- were to rid the area of snakes and rats, something that happens every year.

According to the comments carried by the Turkish Cypriot news agency TAK, Denktash said people would not be settled in the empty town unless Greek Cypriots went ahead with plans to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia.
Tension between the two communities has risen with the decision by the Greek Cypriot-led government to buy the missiles, which parliament approved on Thursday night.

The internationally-recognised Cypriot government says the missiles are defensive but Ankara, which backs the Turkish Cypriot administration, has threatened a military strike if they are placed on the island.

The island has been divided since 1974, when Turkish troops invaded after Greek Cypriots staged a coup backed by the military regime then ruling Greece. Negotiations to unite the two communities in a federation are stalled.
